title: Foreign Language in an English Context

illustrates.quote: Foreign language words or phrases within an English language paragraph are contracted. Use modified letter indicators to represent accented letters. If a modification applies to a letter that would be part of a contraction, do not use the contraction. Use UEB symbols for inverted punctuation.

blocks.features: Single sentence; the foreign (Spanish) word 'trineo' is italicised in the print original (word for sled, no 'spelled'); no accented letters.

braille.notes: One line, verbatim, no line number shown in the source. 'trineo' is contracted like ordinary English text ('.1' marks the italics font/passage indicator; the normal 'in' contraction '9' is used within the word since no accented letter blocks it), per the first sentence of 1.16.3.

printCorrections.was: The word sled is spelled trineo.
printCorrections.evidence: PDF p35 (printed 1-19) page image rendered from references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf: the Example 1-18 box reads "The word for sled is trineo." with trineo in italics; there is no word "spelled" and "for" is present. Source text line 1213 braille ",! ^w = sl$ is .1tr9eo4" is consistent (= is the word "for"). Italics marked with the *...* markup the builder's parseCellMarkup reads.

resolution: Both runs agree on wording; the italics/font handling ('.1' passage indicator) is text feeding straight into liblouis's own UEB translation, not an Emboss format-layer decision -- built as a single para block, letting liblouis's real translation decide contraction use (F-68). Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
